decision: I approved the build with readiness 'ready_with_gaps'
I used the installed DocumentDB skills and Microsoft Learn documentation instead of the unavailable Azure AI best-practices tool.
alternatives: Continue retrying the Azure best-practices tool
reason: Capability discovery failed twice; stop retrying and ground the implementation in the available first-party guidance.
evidence: azure_get_azure_bestpractices returned 'Error: Function failed.' on both attempts.

decision: I chose an API-only Python Flask app with POST /search and no automatic resource provisioning or live writes in this run.
reason: The prompt requires Flask and /search; the readiness corrections require an existing cluster and prohibit writes. Scripts will be provided for subsequent user-authorized execution.
evidence: guidance_for_builder: 'Start with an API-only Flask app against an existing managed cluster ... This run permits no writes'.

decision: I chose Python 3.11+ source compatibility, Flask 3.1.2, synchronous PyMongo 4.15.3, OpenAI SDK 2.8.1, and python-dotenv 1.2.1, testing on installed Python 3.14.10.
reason: Flask and Python are requested; synchronous SDKs keep the example short. Exact direct dependency pins are author defaults chosen for reproducibility and will be installed and tested on the available runtime.
evidence: Review assumes Python 3.11 / Flask 3.x / synchronous PyMongo 4.x; readiness asks to pin versions after validation; python --version returned Python 3.14.10.

decision: I chose native SCRAM-SHA-256 via the portal-issued DOCUMENTDB_URI and public OpenAI via OPENAI_API_KEY, loaded from environment or a locally user-created ignored .env.
reason: The prompt does not select a provider or auth method; the review defaults are the simplest local sample. Production should prefer Entra/managed identity and least-privilege users. No credentials will be generated or copied from MCP.
evidence: Review assumptions: 'native SCRAM-SHA-256 ... DOCUMENTDB_URI ... OPENAI_API_KEY' and 'Use the public OpenAI API'.

decision: I chose a process-wide thread-safe MongoClient with portal SRV URI, TLS and certificate validation enforced, SCRAM-SHA-256, retryWrites=false, default pool sizing, and a 30-second overall database operation budget.
reason: Readiness overrides contradictory skill examples with the official vector quickstart. The 30-second operation budget is an author default for a small local synchronous API; pool sizes remain defaults because no concurrency measurements exist.
evidence: guidance_for_builder: 'Use one PyMongo MongoClient per process, the portal-issued mongodb+srv URI, TLS, and retryWrites=false'; quickstart-python-select-algorithm confirms false.

decision: I chose retail.products with one bounded document per product, stable string _id, title, description, USD price, category, schemaVersion, normalized embedding and embedding model/dimension/version metadata, with no shard key or sharding.
reason: The review's small-catalog default needs neither joins nor horizontal partitioning. Colocating bounded product data and vectors follows the data-modeling skill. Price is illustrative JSON numeric data, not checkout accounting.
evidence: Review data model assumption: 'retail ... products ... stable _id ... embedding ... metadata; no collection sharding'; documentdb-data-modeling principle: 'Data that is accessed together should be stored together.'

decision: I chose text-embedding-ada-002 for both title-plus-description ingestion and query embedding, validating 1536 finite numeric elements and L2-normalizing both paths, with no chat model.
reason: The requested model is fixed; skill guidance requires consistent normalization and metadata. The readiness report establishes 1536 dimensions.
evidence: Prompt: 'Embed product titles and descriptions using text-embedding-ada-002'; readiness: 'with a 1,536-element numeric vector'; documentdb-vector-search/vector-normalize-embeddings.md.

decision: I chose a single custom embedding_ivf index with embedding:cosmosSearch, kind vector-ivf, dimensions 1536, similarity COS, numLists 1, plus the built-in unique _id index; search uses $search/cosmosSearch k=10 and nProbes=1 with searchScore projection.
reason: IVF is requested and supported on M10+; one list covers all 20 demo vectors. No other index supports a requested query. IVF uses nProbes, not DiskANN lSearch.
evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/documentdb/vector-search: 'small demo ... numLists set to 1'; IVF query uses cosmosSearch and searchScore; nProbes defaults to 1 and cannot exceed numLists.

decision: I chose 20 synthetic JSON products, non-destructive stable-ID upserts that skip unchanged embeddings, data-before-index ordering, index-definition conflict detection, and a bounded readiness probe requiring 10 scored results.
reason: Idempotent seeding avoids duplicate products and unnecessary embedding costs. The official Python example seeds before indexing and warns index construction can take minutes; a probe checks behavior rather than claiming training rules that documentation does not establish.
evidence: Review sample-data assumption: 'roughly 20 synthetic products ... idempotent seed script'; quickstart-python-vector-search seeds then indexes; readiness notes index training/ordering semantics are not established.

decision: I chose standard-library unittest offline tests with dependency injection, JSON-only POST requests, a 2000-character query limit, a 16 KiB body limit, generic upstream errors, and a public OpenAI 30-second timeout with no SDK retries.
reason: Offline verification is possible without secrets and cannot accidentally write to a cluster. Limits and generic errors are small-demo defaults to constrain spend and avoid secret-bearing exception output; no authentication or UI is added.
evidence: Readiness requires mocked tests until credentials and permissions exist; HTTP error contract and test acceptance criteria are author choices.

decision: I used the Windows virtual-environment Python path instead of the POSIX path for dependency installation.
reason: The virtual environment was created, but the POSIX executable is not present; the inventory identifies a Windows runtime.
evidence: run_command: 'NOT INSTALLED: .venv/bin/python was not found on PATH.' Readiness Git version is windows.4.

decision: I used an isolated workspace .packages target for dependency verification rather than the runner's pre-populated virtual environment.
alternatives: Change pins to satisfy unrelated agent packages
reason: The invoked virtual-environment executable resolved to an environment containing unrelated Azure agent packages. Isolating the sample packages avoids mixing those dependencies; the documented user workflow remains a fresh venv.
evidence: pip reported agent-framework-openai 1.18.2 requires openai>=2.25.0 and azure-ai-projects 2.11.0 requires openai>=3.0.0; sample pins openai==2.8.1.

decision: I used mocked query/index validation and deferred managed-service acceptance instead of inspecting or changing the unrelated MCP database.
alternatives: Assume MCP credentials supply application credentials
reason: Read-only discovery shows only an unrelated database; no chosen retail cluster, URI, OpenAI key, or write permission is supplied. The run prohibits writes, so the sample's index cannot be created or queried live here.
evidence: documentdb_list_databases returned only sales_forecast_db; readiness: 'No application URI, chosen cluster, database privileges, or network reachability is established' and 'This run permits no writes'.

decision: I chose to document an illustrative development cluster of M10, 32 GiB per shard, one shard, HA Disabled in eastus2, without deploying it or shipping infrastructure.
reason: The review's default fits a 20-product IVF demo and keeps this sample focused on its existing-cluster API. Regional capacity and actual cluster configuration must be confirmed by the user; this is not a production recommendation.
evidence: Review target assumption explicitly lists M10, 32 GiB, one shard, HA Disabled, eastus2; deployment skill's dev example matches these settings; resource changes are prohibited.

decision: I chose to validate cached embeddings without renormalizing them on every seed run, preserving their exact stored values.
alternatives: Renormalize cached vectors and replace every time
reason: Repeated floating-point normalization can introduce tiny changes and unnecessary writes; stored version-1 vectors are already normalized during creation.
evidence: The idempotent seed design should skip unchanged data; floating-point arithmetic can change bitwise values on repeated normalization.

decision: I used the file-write tool for the seed correction instead of a quoted Python replacement command.
reason: The runner's quoting produced a syntax error before editing; direct file writing avoids shell-specific escaping.
evidence: python -c replacement failed: SyntaxError: unterminated string literal (detected at line 1).

decision: I used tls=True and explicit false certificate/hostname relaxation flags without tlsInsecure, and added a real offline PyMongo constructor check.
reason: Actual PyMongo rejects tlsInsecure even when false if tlsAllowInvalidHostnames is also specified. The remaining flags enforce validation; a URI containing tlsInsecure will fail rather than relax security.
evidence: pymongo.errors.InvalidURI: 'URI options tlsInsecure and tlsAllowInvalidHostnames cannot be specified simultaneously.' Constructor used connect=False and made no database operation.

decision: I used an offline regression test with an in-memory generated throwaway password and username to validate real PyMongo constructor options, instead of repeating the credential-free constructor command.
alternatives: Third retry of the failing constructor command
reason: After removing the incompatible TLS flag, SCRAM validation correctly requires a username. An in-memory throwaway credential allows constructor-only validation without network calls or writing credentials to files.
evidence: Second constructor probe failed with 'pymongo.errors.ConfigurationError: SCRAM-SHA-256 requires a username'.
